uses.source_location: p125, final numerical definition/example; p126, Proposition2(b)
uses.attributed_claim:
Bernardi's numerical argument uses a precomplete equivalence
relation $R$ on $\N$: for every partial recursive function $f$
there is a total recursive function $g$ such that
$f(n)\mathord\downarrow$ implies $f(n)\,R\,g(n)$.
For such a relation, distinct equivalence classes are recursively
inseparable; consequently the same holds for disjoint nonempty
unions of classes. The relation $\equiv_{\PA}$ on indices defined
in \eqref{eq:uniform} is one of his examples
\cite[pp.~125--126]{Bernardi}.
The argument above obtains $A,B$ from
Corollary~\ref{cor:source-conditionals} and uses finite PA-proofs to
establish $A\subseteq P_T$ and $B\subseteq N_T$.
uses.support_explanation: The source defines numerical precompleteness exactly as totalization modulo R, lists PA-provable equality of program indices, and states distinct classes recursively inseparable. The manuscript consequence for disjoint nonempty unions follows by selecting one class in each; a separator of unions would separate those classes.

uses.attributed_claim:

\cite[Remark 3.1]{Montagna}.

uses.attributed_claim:
Use the deterministic computation coding for Kleene's trace
predicate as in \cite[p.~115, Note~1]{Montagna}.
Let $e,x,t$ range over $\N$, and write
$\mathsf{Tr}(e,x,t)$ for the primitive-recursive predicate
that $t$ is a halting computation trace with index $e$ and input
$x$, and let $\mathsf{out}:\N\to\N$ be the primitive-recursive
output-extraction function. Put
\[
 G(e,x,y)\equiv
 \exists t\,\bigl(\mathsf{Tr}(e,x,t)\land\mathsf{out}(t)=y\bigr),
 \qquad G_e(x,y)=G(\bar e,x,y).
\]
Primitive-recursive symbols abbreviate their defining formulas in
PA, as in \cite[p.~644]{DPM}; the expanded graph formula is $\Sigma_1$.
For $X,Y\in\mathsf O$, let $\mathcal I(X,Y)=\N$.
An index $e\in\mathcal I(X,Y)$ is interpreted using
$\gamma_X$ for inputs and $\gamma_Y$ for outputs.
uses.support_explanation: The PR-extension notation paragraph explains how formulas with primitive-recursive symbols are replaced by formulas of PA preserving free variables and provability. The Σ1 graph formula in the manuscript is its explicit deterministic trace construction; it is not a quotation of DPM.

uses.source_location: §1 p646, definitions of objects and uniform equality; Montagna pp105–106
uses.attributed_claim:
Montagna's objects are the sets generated from $\N$ by
Cartesian products and the displayed disjoint unions
\cite[p.~105]{Montagna}. Let $S_T^{\mathrm{set}}$ denote that
presentation of the unprimed category, using the computation
formulas and the induced numerical codings fixed above
\cite{Montagna,DPM}. There is a functor
\[
 \Pi_T:S_T\longrightarrow S_T^{\mathrm{set}},\qquad
 \Pi_T(X)=|X|,\qquad \Pi_T([e]_T)=[e]_T^{\mathrm{set}}.
\]
Every object of $S_T^{\mathrm{set}}$ is $|X|$ for a term
$X\in\mathsf O$, and the map on each hom-set is a bijection
because both presentations use \eqref{eq:uniform} with the same
numerical codings. Thus $\Pi_T$ is an equivalence. For $T=\PA$,
the target is Montagna's unprimed category $S$ with these choices
of computation formulas and codings.
uses.support_explanation: DPM extends Montagna’s set-based unprimed presentation to T. Object terms versus their interpreted sets are the manuscript’s explicit equivalent presentation, not a new assertion attributed verbatim to DPM. Uniform function equality matches graph equivalence using PA-provable functionality.

uses.attributed_claim:
Composition is written $gf=g\circ f$, so $f$ is applied first.
A \emph{restriction category} is a category equipped with an assignment
that sends every morphism
$f:X\rightharpoonup Y$ to a morphism
$\bar f:X\rightharpoonup X$ satisfying
\[
 f\bar f=f,\qquad
 \bar f\bar g=\bar g\bar f,\qquad
 \overline{g\bar f}=\bar g\bar f,\qquad
 \bar h f=f\overline{hf}.
\]
In the middle two equations $g:X\rightharpoonup Z$; in the last,
$h:Y\rightharpoonup Z$ \cite{CockettLack}.
The morphisms $\bar f$ are idempotent and are called
\emph{restriction idempotents}, also called domains
\cite[Section~5]{Heller}.
The morphism $f$ is \emph{total} when $\bar f=1_X$.
The total morphisms form a subcategory, denoted by
$\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal C)$ for a restriction category $\mathcal C$.
A \emph{restriction functor} $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between
restriction categories satisfies $F(\bar f)=\overline{F(f)}$ for every
morphism $f$. A \emph{restriction equivalence} consists of restriction
functors in both directions whose composites are naturally isomorphic
to the respective identity functors.
uses.support_explanation: Heller calls endomorphisms equal to their domains domains; domdomφ=domφ and φ=φdomφ appear in the domain calculus. Restriction-idempotent is the current Cockett–Lack terminology, accurately identified with Heller’s domains.

uses.attributed_claim:
For $f:X\rightharpoonup Y$ and a restriction idempotent $a$ on $Y$,
the \emph{inverse image} of $a$ is the restriction idempotent
$f^*a=\overline{af}$ on $X$.
A restriction idempotent $r$ on $Y$ \emph{receives} $f$ when $rf=f$
\cite[Section 6]{Heller}.
The \emph{range} $\ran(f)$ is the least restriction idempotent receiving $f$;
we require the agreement law
\[
 gf=hf\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 g\ran(f)=h\ran(f)
 \qquad(g,h:Y\rightharpoonup Z).
\]
For an ordinary partial function $f$, the restriction idempotent
$\bar f$ and the range $\ran(f)$ are the partial identities on its
domain of definition and image, respectively.
uses.support_explanation: The source explicitly defines ε receiving φ by εφ=φ, and range by the arrow-agreement property before observing leastness. V29 preserves that substantive agreement law. Its inverse-image typing is correct; see source-typo note in report.

uses.attributed_claim:
A \emph{Turing morphism} on $U$ is a morphism
$\tau:U\times U\rightharpoonup U$ such that, for every object $X$
and every $f:X\times U\rightharpoonup U$, there is a total
parameter map $r:X\to U$ satisfying
\[
 f=\tau(r\times1_U).
\]
A \emph{recursion category} here is a prodominical isotypical
category with binary restriction products and a Turing morphism,
as in \cite[Section 9]{Heller}.
uses.support_explanation: Heller defines a Turing morphism W×X→Y by parameterization of arbitrary V×X→Y using a total V→W, and a recursion category as a prodominical isotype with such a morphism. V29 takes W=X=Y=U; its extra mention of binary restriction products records the P-category structure.

uses.source_location: §3 p1256, frame definition continuing on p1257
uses.attributed_claim:
Define an object $V:J\to\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$ of $\mathcal E$
by the following objects $V_j=V(j)$ and morphisms
$r_i^V=V(0\to i)$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:universal-fork}
 \begin{gathered}
 V_0=\N^4,\qquad V_1=V_2=\N^2,\\
 r_1^V:V_0\to V_1,\qquad r_1^V(k,z,a,b)=(k,a),\\
 r_2^V:V_0\to V_2,\qquad r_2^V(k,z,a,b)=(k,b).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
We regard $V$ also as an object of $\mathcal A$, whose objects
are those of $\mathcal E$.
For an object $A=(m,A_0)$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$, put
$m(A)=m$. Thus $|A|\subseteq\N^{m(A)}$,
$m(V_0)=4$, and $m(V_1)=m(V_2)=2$.
Fix recursive numerical encodings of nonempty finite sequences of tuples,
\[
 \operatorname{code}_m:
 \coprod_{n\ge1}(\N^m)^n\xrightarrow{\cong}W_m\subseteq\N
 \qquad(m\ge0),
\]
where each $W_m$ is recursive and the length and entry operations
are recursive. For an object $A$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$, put
\[
 A^\#=\{\operatorname{code}_{m(A)}(a_1,\ldots,a_n):
                 n\ge1,\ a_1,\ldots,a_n\in A\}\subseteq W_{m(A)}.
\]
This is a c.e.\ numerical carrier. Let $V^\#$ have components
$(V^\#)_j=(V_j)^\#$.
Its map $(V^\#)(0\to i):(V_0)^\#\to(V_i)^\#$ decodes a sequence,
applies $r_i^V$ to each entry, and encodes the resulting sequence,
for $i=1,2$.
Choose isomorphisms in $\mathcal E$
$V\cong V\times V$, $V\cong V+V$, and $V\cong V^\#$.
Together with their inverses, these form a \emph{frame} at $V$
\cite[Section 3]{Heller}.
Let $\mathscr R_X$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$
on the objects obtained from $V$ by finitely many applications of
the chosen binary restriction products, binary coproducts, and
nonempty-word formation.
The isomorphisms, constructed in Lemma~\ref{lem:fork-frames}, make
$\mathscr R_X$ isotypical.
uses.support_explanation: A frame consists of chosen isomorphisms X→X×X, X→X+X, X→X# and their inverses. V29 lists exactly those six maps. Existence of its concrete fork isomorphisms is proved locally and is not supplied by Heller.

uses.source_location: p108, first paragraph and Turing-morphism paragraph; p115, Note1
uses.attributed_claim:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:arithmetized-evaluation}
For this computation coding, there are an index $u\in\N$ and
primitive-recursive functions
$\operatorname{s},\operatorname{comp}:\N^2\to\N$
such that PA proves functionality
of $G$ and the universal closures of
\begin{align}
 G_u(\langle e,x\rangle,y)
   &\leftrightarrow G(e,x,y),
   \label{eq:arithmetized-universal}\\
 G(\operatorname{s}(e,a),x,y)
   &\leftrightarrow G(e,\langle a,x\rangle,y),
   \label{eq:arithmetized-specialization}\\
 G(\operatorname{comp}(f,e),x,z)
   &\leftrightarrow
     \exists y\,\bigl(G(e,x,y)\land G(f,y,z)\bigr).
   \label{eq:composition}
\end{align}
Regard $u$ as an element of $\mathcal I(\omega\times\omega,\omega)$.
For each fixed $e\in\N$, there is an index
$k_e\in\N$ for which PA proves
\[
 \forall a\forall p\,
 \bigl(G_{k_e}(a,p)\leftrightarrow
       p=\operatorname{s}(\bar e,a)\bigr).
\]
In particular, PA proves $\forall a\exists!p\,G_{k_e}(a,p)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
These are the formalized enumeration, composition, and
parameterization properties of the computation coding used in
\cite[p.~108; p.~115, Note~1]{Montagna}.
The pairing can be replaced by the pairing fixed above, using
the PA-provable inverse equations for the two numerical codings.
For $k_e$, use an index for the primitive-recursive function
$a\mapsto\operatorname{s}(e,a)$; its defining equation and
totality are provable in PA.
\end{proof}
uses.support_explanation: The source asserts the pointed p-category structure, the universal evaluator, and formalized s-m-n; Note1 fixes its arithmetic graph formulas. This supports the standard formalized construction used by the lemma. It does not print all displayed uniform functionality/composition/specialization graph equations separately.
uses.precision_note: For fully explicit provenance of every displayed PA theorem, cite a formalized enumeration/composition theorem or add a short proof for the chosen coding. Do not say Montagna states all these equations verbatim.

\emph{Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition}
\cite[Corollary 2]{Composition} proves that the proposed composition
is not independent of representatives for any consistent c.e.\
extension $T$ of $\PA$. Thus these primed systems do not define
categories with that composition.
uses.support_explanation: Montagna’s primed equality requires, for each standard input, a PA proof of the same convergence/output statement. It agrees with DPM’s T=PA specialization. V29 correctly rejects the original category claim on the independent Composition result.

uses.source_location: p109, displayed(*) and following proof via Feferman Theorem2.13
uses.attributed_claim:
For $X\in\mathsf O$ and a $\Sigma_1$ arithmetic formula $C(x)$,
where $x$ is the numerical code variable for $X$, choose
a witness-search index $j_C$ for which
\[
 \PA\vdash\forall x\forall y\,
 \bigl(G_{j_C}(x,y)\leftrightarrow(C(x)\land y=x)\bigr).
\]
Such an index searches increasing bounds for a witness to $C(x)$
and returns $x$ when a witness is found
\cite[p.~109, equation~$(*)$]{Montagna}. Write
$[C]_T=[j_C]_T:X\rightharpoonup X$.
For two such formulas,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:domain-order}
 [C]_T\le[D]_T
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T\vdash\forall x\,(C(x)\longrightarrow D(x)).
\end{equation}
Conjunction and disjunction give meets and joins of restriction
idempotents. For $[e]_T:X\rightharpoonup Y$, its restriction
$\overline{[e]_T}$ and range $\ran([e]_T)$ are represented respectively by
\[
 \exists y\,G_e(x,y),\qquad
 R_e(y):=\exists x\,G_e(x,y).
\]
For a restriction idempotent $[C]_T:Y\rightharpoonup Y$, the
equation $[C]_T[e]_T=[e]_T$ holds precisely when
$T$ proves $G_e(x,y)\to C(y)$ universally, equivalently when
$T$ proves $R_e(y)\to C(y)$ universally.
Write $g=[p]_T,h=[q]_T:Y\rightharpoonup Z$.
If $g[e]_T=h[e]_T$, the
composition equation and PA-provable functionality of $G_e$ give
\[
 T\vdash\forall y\forall z\,
 \bigl(R_e(y)\longrightarrow
       (G_p(y,z)\leftrightarrow G_q(y,z))\bigr).
\]
Indeed, a witness $x$ to $R_e(y)$ can be used in the equality of
the composite graphs, and functionality identifies the intermediate
output with $y$. This proves $g[R_e]_T=h[R_e]_T$ in $S_T$.
The index $j_{R_e}$ is independent of the theory, so its class
represents the range over every extension of $T$.
uses.support_explanation: The source explicitly constructs an index whose PA-provable domain is any specified Σ1 formula and whose output, when defined, is the input. This is equivalent to V29’s PA-provable graph identity. The subsequent restriction/range argument is proved in V29 itself.

uses.attributed_claim:
We also apply the criterion to the syntactic recursion categories of
Montagna and Di Paola--Montagna \cite{Montagna,DPM}.
For a consistent computably enumerable (c.e.)
extension $T$ of Peano arithmetic ($\PA$), the morphisms of $S_T$ are
equivalence classes of indices of partial recursive functions. Two
indices are identified when $T$ proves the universal closure of the
equivalence of their graph formulas. These categories are not locally
connected \cite[Corollary 4.4]{DPM}. Interpretation in all models of
$T$ with carrier $\N$ gives a faithful range functor into a locally
connected product of partial-map categories. Partial recursive functions
selecting between predicates proved complementary in $T$ represent the
required section lifts.
The construction commutes with theory extension.
The total restriction splitting of $S_T$ also realizes the
first-order syntax and theory construction of
Appendix~\ref{app:syntax-theories}
(Theorem~\ref{thm:syntactic-generated-theory}).
Its universal properties use $T$-provable graph equality.
uses.support_explanation: The cited source introduces the unprimed syntactic p-recursion category S based on PA-provable equality. V29 applies its own generalized criterion to that unprimed construction and DPM’s extensions.

uses.attributed_claim:
Di Paola and Heller proved recursive inseparability in dominical
recursion categories in which every morphism has a section
\cite[Theorem 8.15]{DPH}. Bernardi obtained categorical inseparability
results from precomplete equivalence relations, including PA-provable
equality of partial recursive functions among his examples
\cite[pp.~125--128]{Bernardi}.
Montagna also obtained effectively inseparable pairs in his syntactic
category $S$
\cite[Remark 3.1]{Montagna}.
uses.support_explanation: Remark3.1 explicitly concludes effectively inseparable domain pairs exist in S (and claims S′ as well). V29 restricts the attribution to S, so it avoids perpetuating the later-invalidated primed category assertion.
